name: file-type-icon
title: File type icon
description: A file icon picked from the extension or MIME type, drawn in the library's own style, with the extension as a small label.
docs: Pass name ('report-final.xlsx'), mime ('application/pdf') or both: the extension in the name wins (it has to look like one, up to eight letters and digits with at least one letter and no spaces, so 'Invoice no. 4821' has none), then the MIME type, then its first part (image/, video/, audio/, text/). You get a page with a folded corner, a glyph and a dark tag with the extension (up to five letters). The families are document, sheet, slide, image, video, audio, archive, code and unknown, and each has a glyph of its own (lines, a grid, a screen, hills, a play mark, a waveform, a zipper, brackets, a question mark), so none is told apart by colour alone. size is sm, md (default) or lg: 28, 40 and 64px wide. sm leaves the tag off, which would be too small to read, and draws the glyph larger; showExtension overrides that either way. FILE_TYPES (extension to family) and MIME_TYPES (MIME type to extension) are plain exported objects: add your own at startup, FILE_TYPES.blend = 'image', and every icon follows. family forces a family, and fileTypeLabel(name, mime) gives 'PDF document' for a label. The icon is hidden from assistive technology unless you pass a label, because the file name beside it carries the meaning. It is a server component: no script is shipped.
